extracted.intended_audience: advertising agencies, creative teams and brand/marketing professionals submitting work to Cannes Lions Direct
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and judging criteria for entering work into the Cannes Lions Direct awards, including category definitions, entry restrictions, and the judging weightings used to evaluate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted and response-driven creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Direct Lions celebrate targeted and response-driven creativity. The work should demonstrate how insights and/or data were used as part of the strategy to engage specific target audience groups and develop customer relationships, inspiring action and producing measurable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must show use of insights/data in strategy to engage specific target audiences, build customer relationships, inspire action and deliver measurable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging weightings
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of criteria will be considered during judging, weighted as follows: 30% idea; 20% strategy; 20% execution; 30% impact and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are evaluated primarily on idea and impact/results (each 30%), with strategy and execution each 20%; entrants should present material aligned to these weighted dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry frequency and section restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work can be entered up to four times in Direct. However, the same piece of work may only be entered once in ‘A. Direct: Sectors’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage multiple entries carefully; you may submit the same work across up to four Direct entries but only once into the sector (A) section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtitles recommendation for films
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtitles are highly recommended on all case films, films, demo films and original content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide subtitles on film content to improve accessibility and judge comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: A: Direct — sector entries may be submitted only once in section
rubrics_metrics.description: The same entry can be submitted only once in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within section A (Sectors) do not submit duplicate sector entries for the same work.

rubrics_metrics.name: A01 Consumer Goods
rubrics_metrics.description: All fast-moving and durable consumer goods, including but not limited to food and beverages, toiletries, cleaning products, other household goods, other FMCGs, clothing and accessories, furniture, and consumer electronics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast-food entries should be entered into A04 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: A02 Healthcare
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharma, OTC drugs, wellness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work has been created for a Charity/NFP then this should be entered into A07.

rubrics_metrics.name: A03 Automotive
rubrics_metrics.description: Vehicles, other automobiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: A04 Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains
rubrics_metrics.description: All transport- and travel-related services, including public transport and tourism boards. All entertainment- and leisure-related services, including museums, festivals and gyms. All shops, including online shopping, opticians, hairdressers and estate agents. All restaurants and fast food chains, including cafés and bars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fast-food entries (entered here rather than A01).

rubrics_metrics.name: A05 Media/Entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Music, film, television, publications and media, books, news, digital platforms and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: A06 Consumer Services/Business to Business
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercial public services, legal, financial, B2B technology, consultancies and professional services, other business services, internal and corporate communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: A07 Not-for-Profit / Charity / Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Government, public information, NGOs, military, charities, non-profit organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All not-for-profit, charity or government work should be entered in the relevant sector and/or A07. Corporate social responsibility work should be entered in the relevant sector and/or F07.

rubrics_metrics.name: B01 Mailing/Programmatic Mail
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating targeted and programmatic mailing campaigns. The work in this category should demonstrate efficiency in the technology and processes used, effective placement and evidence of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please send physical samples for the jury to experience; demonstrate technological/process efficiency and evidence of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: B02 Small-Scale Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-mail and print collateral, including small physical objects and all other hand-held (or equivalent in size) items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Small-scale' refers to the physical size of the ambient item, not the scale of the distribution. Please send physical samples for the jury to experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: B03 Large-Scale Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-traditional media. This includes but is not limited to direct response stunts, street teams, direct response events, outdoor/ambient media and other mediums that encourage direct interaction and seek a measurable response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Large-scale' refers to the physical size of the ambient item, not the scale of the distribution. Please send physical samples for the jury to experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: B04 Use of Broadcast
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct work using cinema, TV or radio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how the chosen medium led the other direct elements within the work (i.e., how broadcast informed or drove the direct campaign).

rubrics_metrics.name: B05 Use of Print/Outdoor
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct work using print or outdoor. This may include, but is not limited to, newspapers, magazines, inserts, trade journals, traditional billboard or poster sites, bus shelters and transit advertising using standard advertising space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augmented billboards should be entered into B03 (Channels: Large-Scale Media).

rubrics_metrics.name: C: Data & Technology — overall expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Work driven by the creative use of data or technology that enhanced the customer experience and led to measurable business results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must show how data/technology enhanced experience and resulted in measurable business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: C01 Data-Driven Direct Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The application of data and insights that significantly forms the basis of the direct strategy, demonstrating how the data-driven strategy helped to profile customers’ behaviours and segmentation, that ultimately led to successful direct marketing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how data/insights formed the strategy, profiling, segmentation and led to successful direct marketing outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: C02 Data-Driven Targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Work where the interpretation and analysis of data was used to build a targeted communication for a specific audience. This may include but is not limited to, hyper-targeting, precision targeting, audience mapping and targeting segmentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how data interpretation produced a targeted communication strategy for a defined audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: C03 Use of Real-Time Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Work where real-time data creatively enhanced engagement with a target audience or was utilised in promoting an ongoing relationship with the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should clearly demonstrate how the use of real-time data led to measurable and meaningful results.

rubrics_metrics.name: C04 New Realities & Emerging Tech
rubrics_metrics.description: The creative application of immersive experiences that push the boundaries of technology within direct strategies to engage and strengthen relationships with consumers. This could include, but not be limited to, AR, VR, XR, wearable tech and mobile devices, GPS, NFC, facial recognition, voice technology, blockchain technology, gamification, virtual worlds, the metaverse and all other emerging platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include prototypes of early-stage technology; focus on implemented creative tech that enhanced direct strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: C05 Gaming
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating the use of gaming and games to effectively target a specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how the chosen game or gaming platform drove engagement and brand affinity within the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: D: Digital & Social — overall expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital and social mediums/techniques used as a piece of direct communication for a brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should show how digital/social mediums were used as direct communications to enhance relationships with specific audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: D01 Use of Digital Platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that uses online platforms or associated technologies to enhance relationships with a specific audience. This may include, but is not limited to, websites, games, search engines, ecommerce platforms, banner ads and instant messaging, mobile apps etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include prototypes of early-stage technology. Social media-led work should be entered in D03, D04 and D05 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: D02 Use of Mobile
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted communication work delivered through mobile/portable devices such as mobile phones, mobile technology, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how mobile delivery targeted and engaged a specific audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: D03 Use of Social Platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that uses social media, streaming platforms, blogs, Wikis, video-sharing sites, hosted services etc. to create and/or enhance relationships with a community/consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work entered in this category should be planned and executed on social platforms as opposed to campaigns that went social.

rubrics_metrics.name: D04 Real-Time Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted social activity that responds to world events, public affairs and other real-world, real-time activity prompting social sharing and a measurable response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate timeliness, relevance and measurable response resulting from real-time social activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: D05 Co-Creation & User-Generated Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Social activity designed to encourage a community/fanbase to contribute to or collaborate with a brand initiative through a clear call to action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the initiative solicited contributions, the clarity of call to action, and measurable engagement/results from user-generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: E: Excellence in Direct — overall expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories that recognise outstanding craft and execution in specific disciplines of direct work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should showcase craft excellence that directly contributed to measured response and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: E01 Copywriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Work showcasing outstanding copywriting skill that has led to a successful and measured response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how copywriting contributed to effectiveness and measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: E02 Art Direction/Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that showcases the outstanding design of a customer experience that has led to a successful and measured response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show design choices and their role in driving the measured response.

rubrics_metrics.name: E03 Experience Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Work showcasing outstanding design in the customer experience that has led to a successful and measured response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight user journey, touchpoints and how experience design produced results.

rubrics_metrics.name: E04 Launch/Relaunch
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct marketing campaigns created to launch or relaunch a product or service on the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can include work aiming to acquire new customers, and reinvigorate lapsed customers; show objectives and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: E05 Personalised Campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Dynamic work based on consumer data and insight. This includes but is not limited to content from websites, videos, emails, social and blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how the campaign enriched the user’s experience by driving engagement and achieving results.

rubrics_metrics.name: F: Culture & Context — overall expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that is brought to life through cultural insights and regional context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must demonstrate cultural insight or regional context that materially informed the creative solution and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: F01 Local Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Work for brands distributed solely within a specific locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should resonate with a clearly defined, local target audience; explain locality-specific strategy and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: F02 Challenger Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their approach in response to competitor pressure by challenging the status quo to create game-changing work that uses progressive thinking and innovative creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the brand challenged category norms and achieved impact through inventive strategy and creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: F03 Single-Market Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that aired or ran in a single country / region / market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should describe how the campaign was designed for the specific target market and demonstrate market-specific results.

rubrics_metrics.name: F04 Social Behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work inspired by a specific audience or community, relying on identifiable social behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how leveraging insights into consumer behaviour created a powerful connection with the brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: F05 Use of Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that celebrates the art of humour in branded communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should show how wit, satire or cleverness produced memorable connections and contributed to results.

rubrics_metrics.name: F06 Breakthrough on a Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative use of modest budgets and/or resources in relation to the market and/or industry to create maximum impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how insight, smart spending and strategic thinking solved a business problem despite limited resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: F07 Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose-driven work/brand activism that addresses social, ethical and environmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how the brand’s purpose created value and affected communities by connecting customers to culture. Corporate social responsibility work should also be considered against relevant sector categories and/or A07.

rubrics_metrics.name: F08 Market Disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their strategy in response to local / regional / global issues, embracing new ways of delivering their brand while showing consideration for the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show strategic adaptation to contextual issues and the resulting consumer impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: F09 Cultural Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work crafted around strategic solutions rooted in the lived experiences of culturally grounded communities. Work which reflects and translates the nuances of customs, behaviours, and traditions that shape foundational perspectives on identity (e.g. disability, gender, race, orientation, age).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate how cultural nuance informed strategy and execution and drove growth and impact.
